Choose the Rank of Bayesian PCA Imputation on Held-Out Values

Source: R/mi_pca_tune.R
mipca_tune.Rd

Hide a set of observed values, fit mipca() at each candidate rank, and score how well each rank's draws predict the hidden values. Pass the result to mipca_fit() to fit the best rank.

Usage

mipca_tune(
  obj,
  rank,
  na_loc = NULL,
  n_cols = NULL,
  n_rows = 4L,
  transform,
  n_diag = 10000L,
  iter_warmup = 100L,
  iter_sampling = 100L,
  chains = 4L,
  thin = 1,
  init = 1,
  refresh = 0L,
  spectra = spectra_opts(),
  seed = NULL,
  abb = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'si_tune'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

obj

A double matrix with samples in rows and features in columns. Row and column names are required and must be unique. NA and NaN values are imputed.

rank

Integer vector. The candidate ranks, each a whole number of at least 1, given once.

na_loc

A list or NULL. The values to hold out, as one two-column matrix of row and column positions in a list, the form sample_na_loc() returns with n_reps = 1. Each must be an observed value of obj. With NULL, the positions are drawn from n_cols and n_rows. Defaults to NULL.

n_cols

Integer or NULL. Number of columns that receive held-out values. With NULL, 10% of the columns, at least 50 and at most 500. Defaults to NULL.

n_rows

Integer. Number of held-out values in each of the n_cols columns. Leave it out when na_loc is given. Defaults to 4.

transform

Character or a transform object. The scale the model is fitted on: "identity", "logit_biwhiten", or an object from tf_identity(), tf_sv() or tf_biwhiten(). See Details in mipca().

n_diag

Integer. Number of missing values, held-out values included, on which Rhat and ESS are computed for each rank. They are sampled across columns with few and with many missing values. Defaults to 10000.

iter_warmup

Integer. Number of iterations discarded at the start of each chain, 0 or more. Defaults to 100.

iter_sampling

Integer. Number of draws kept per chain. Defaults to 100.

chains

Integer. Number of independent chains. Defaults to 4.

thin

Integer. After warmup, each chain keeps one iteration in every thin, so it runs iter_sampling * thin iterations to keep iter_sampling draws. Defaults to 1.

init

Numeric. How widely each chain's starting values are spread: each missing value starts at a random draw whose standard deviation is init times its column's observed standard deviation. Must be positive. Defaults to 1.

refresh

Integer. Print a progress line every refresh iterations of each chain, or 0 for none. Defaults to 0.

spectra

A spectra_opts object. Settings for the eigensolver, from spectra_opts().

seed

Integer, numeric, or NULL. Seed for the held-out values and the sampler. With NULL, both are drawn from R's random number stream. Defaults to NULL.

abb

Optional character or integer vector. Columns to draw by approximate Bayesian bootstrap instead of by the model. abb_cols() proposes them. Defaults to NULL.

x

A si_tune object.

...

Not used.

Value

A data frame of class si_tune, one row per rank, with columns:

  • rank: the rank.

  • crps: the mean score of the held-out values. Lower is better.

  • implied_nu, implied_lo, implied_hi: the degrees of freedom the held-out values imply, and its 68% bootstrap interval.

  • robust_z: the interquartile range of the standardized held-out values, divided by 1.349. Near 1 for Gaussian noise.

  • ess_min, ess_p10, ess_med: the minimum, 10% quantile and median ESS over the n_diag values.

  • ess_ok: the proportion of them with an ESS of at least 100 * chains.

  • rhat_med, rhat_p90, rhat_max: the median, 90% quantile and maximum Rhat.

  • rhat_ok: the proportion with an Rhat of at most 1.05.

  • ndraws: the number of draws, over all chains.

  • n_diag: the number of values Rhat and ESS were computed on.

  • sigma: a list column, the noise standard deviation at the end of each chain.

  • time: the seconds the rank took.

  • error: the message of a failed fit, or NA.

  • result: a list column, a data frame with one row per held-out value: its row and col, the truth, the mean and sd of its draws, its crps and pit, and truth_lat, mean_lat and sd_lat on the scale the model is fitted on.

  • diag: a list column, a data frame of the row, col, rhat and ess of each of the n_diag values.

The table also carries the transform, the sampler settings, abb and the held-out positions, which mipca_fit() reads.

Details

The held-out values. With na_loc = NULL, sample_na_loc() picks n_cols columns and hides n_rows observed values in each. A column is eligible if it is not constant and has at least n_rows + 2 observed values. Every rank is fitted on the same matrix, with the same values hidden, and is scored on those values only. The holdout needs more than two values. The abb columns take no part in tuning, and no value in them is held out.

The rank. crps is the continuous ranked probability score of each held-out value against its draws, on the scale of obj, averaged over the held-out values. A lower score is better. mipca_fit() fits the rank with the lowest crps unless it is given another.

The noise. implied_nu is the Student-t degrees of freedom that the spread of the held-out values implies, Inf when they look Gaussian. implied_lo and implied_hi are its bootstrap interval. implied_nu is the raw reading. mipca_fit() fits with nu set to implied_nu, or to 5 if the reading is lower.

Failures. A rank whose fit fails does not stop the call. Its row holds the message in error, and its scores are NA.

Reproducibility. With the same seed, the held-out values and the table are the same. A given seed leaves R's random number stream as it was. With seed = NULL, the same set.seed() before the call gives the same table.

See also

  • mipca_fit() to fit a rank from this table.

  • mipca() to fit with a rank and nu of your own.

  • sample_na_loc() to draw held-out positions to pass as na_loc.

Examples

set.seed(1)
sim <- sim_mat(n = 50, p = 20, beta = TRUE)
tuned <- mipca_tune(
  sim$input,
  rank = 1:3,
  transform = "logit_biwhiten",
  n_cols = 10,
  seed = 1
)
tuned
#> si_tune: 3 ranks on a 50 x 20 matrix, holdout 40 cells over 10 columns
#>  rank    crps ess_p10  ess_ok rhat_max implied_nu implied_lo implied_hi  time
#>     1 0.09652   267.0 0.07143    1.032      2.600      2.324      4.215 0.024
#>     2 0.09713   247.1 0.02857    1.040      2.842      2.366      4.286 0.025
#>     3 0.10109   172.0 0.01429    1.052      3.414      2.726      6.308 0.025
#>   next: mipca_fit(x, obj) fits the rank with the lowest crps.
#>         mipca_fit(x, obj, rank) fits another rank.
fit <- mipca_fit(tuned, sim$input, seed = 1)
#> the implied nu at rank 1 is 2.6, under the floor of 5, so the fit uses nu = 5. Pass 'nu' to use another value
#> Chain 1 Iteration:   1 / 200 [  0%] (Warmup)
#> Chain 1 Iteration: 100 / 200 [ 50%] (Warmup)
#> Chain 1 Iteration: 200 / 200 [100%] (Sampling)
#> Chain 1 finished in 0.0 seconds.
#> Chain 2 Iteration:   1 / 200 [  0%] (Warmup)
#> Chain 2 Iteration: 100 / 200 [ 50%] (Warmup)
#> Chain 2 Iteration: 200 / 200 [100%] (Sampling)
#> Chain 2 finished in 0.0 seconds.
#> Chain 3 Iteration:   1 / 200 [  0%] (Warmup)
#> Chain 3 Iteration: 100 / 200 [ 50%] (Warmup)
#> Chain 3 Iteration: 200 / 200 [100%] (Sampling)
#> Chain 3 finished in 0.0 seconds.
#> Chain 4 Iteration:   1 / 200 [  0%] (Warmup)
#> Chain 4 Iteration: 100 / 200 [ 50%] (Warmup)
#> Chain 4 Iteration: 200 / 200 [100%] (Sampling)
#> Chain 4 finished in 0.0 seconds.
fit
#> si_mi fit: 50 x 20, 100 imputed cells, 400 draws
#>   next: as.matrix() with 'draw' for a completed matrix, summary() for Rhat and ESS
